We calculate the duration of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ mode of life, which is the amount of time the system spends in a mixture of its anomalous and normal states before decaying, using three methods. We calculate this lifetime as part of our study of $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay modes that involve conversions, rare decays, and same-flavor oscillations. We determine probable lifetime ranges for these decay modes and assess how they interact with each other and with oscillation phenomena.

This study provides the first detailed examination of Lumi-leasemoitored public Pb-Pb data at 5.02 TeV, examining an earlier discovery of flow fluctuations by the ALICE collaboration, and supplementing their findings with stream angle-dependent intensity fluctuations. Dependence on transverse momentum, centrality, and specific flow coefficients is determined for the stream angle that exhibits the maximum intensity fluctuations, and a distinction is made between instantaneous and average fluctuations. The data covers the most central collisions studied thus far, and a comparison is made with the ALICE collaboration's initial report based on semi-central collisions. The results are also compared with the ALICE collaboration's findings, using a different method to calculate flow fluctuations. The observed fluctuations are found to be similar in magnitude to charge-averaged fluctuations, which could be related to initial conditions or flow magnitude. The potential importance of stream angle-dependent fluctuations for charge separation phenomena, such as the "directionality problem," is also discussed.

In the context of data integration, where data is drawn from multiple sources, discrepancies can arise between source tables caused by differing interpretations of identical concepts. These discrepancies manifest as inconsistencies in the data itself, which must be resolved to create a unified dataset. We are focusing on three types of discrepancies: value discrepancies (differences in numerical data), format discrepancies (dissimilar representations of the same data format), and structural discrepancies (variances in defined relationships between elements). The challenge lies in determining the origin of these discrepancies and selecting an appropriate correction strategy. We are assuming a pre-existing understanding of the intended relationships between data elements, which are captured in a set of functional dependencies. In this study, we outline an approach for addressing discrepancies in tables that contain null values and observe how handling value discrepancies and structural discrepancies is affected by the presence of these values. Furthermore, we examine the impact of employing the Codd relational completeness criterion, which is ensured by a set of specified functional dependencies, in our approach.

We introduce a novel dynamic modeling framework, termed TV-PAR, to forecast count-based time series with broken patterns of past time periods. TV-PAR distinguishes itself from traditional time series models by accounting for temporal variations in parameters and correlations with past time series. This innovative feature enables TV-PAR to effectively capture and adapt to changes in count-based time series, even when those changes occur during the forecasting period. Unlike static models like Poisson AR, our proposed method showcases the benefits of considering temporal variations in parameters and pairwise correlations with real-world data, leading to superior performance in our numerical experiments.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
integrates both local and global information to create robust and invariant
features. NDFs comprise of two components: a neural network that generates
regional descriptors and another that constructs a global field to capture the
object's three-dimensional structure and pose. We employ a novel training
objective that combines both local and global matching to learn object-aware
representations. We show that NDFs outperform existing methods in multiple
object recognition and classification tasks, surpassing the performance of our
baseline by 30%. Moreover, NDFs exhibit robustness under significant pose
variations, surpassing the baseline by 40% in our newly introduced task to
classify objects based on their orientation. We also apply NDFs to a grasping
task, presenting intuitive and successful grasping strategies, and highlight the
scalability of NDFs, capable of handling over 100 object categories with less
computational requirements compared to prevalent pointcloud-based methods.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in both universality classes for N > 2. Specifically, we have determined é (N) and ñ (N) for N = 2, 3, 4, showing that é (N) approximately equals 0. 8 5, while ñ (N) ranges from 0. 9 5 for N = 2 to 0. 8 6 for N = 4. Notably, our results indicate that é (N) is independent of N, while ñ (N) decreases with increasing N.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to compare the performance of various algorithms used to infer parameters from noisy and limited data. This comparison often involves analyzing how effectively each algorithm recovers the underlying data, typically measured by a recovery metric whose expected value can be computed using the estimated parameters. In many cases, especially when working with random data, it is crucial to understand how the expected recovery performance changes as the noise level increases. To this end, we need to examine how the recovery performance changes on average in relation to the noise level, effectively seeking the second moment of the recovery performance. To achieve this, we employ the TAP (Thouless-Anderson-Palmer) free energy framework, a powerful statistical physics tool that enables the calculation of the expected recovery performance and its variance. Building upon the foundation laid by Bissacot, Engel, and Mackenzie, we derived a novel expression that directly yields the variance of the recovery performance for Edwards-Anderson model parameters. This new expression, in turn, allows us to demonstrate the local concavity of the TAP free energy, a key property that facilitates the comparison of recovery performance across different datasets. Consequently, this local concavity also implies a more general phenomenon, the subadditivity of the average recovery performance, which can be observed in synthetic data sets resembling certain real-world scenarios.

The detection of extraterrestrial optical pulses resulting from the interaction of intense laser light with aerosols filling the atmosphere is theoretically possible and would indicate the location of aerosol particles. Originally, this idea was met with skepticism but has since been supported by actual data, suggesting that it may be a viable method for detecting particles in space. Researchers have proposed and are exploring various techniques for using this phenomenon in combination with photometric data to assess aerosol properties, and a recent study has shown that this method may be effective for determining the size of particles even when they are extremely small.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on the architecture: those with a separate correspondence module and those with a single unified network. In the single-unity network category, research has been done to incorporate additional object features to enhance performance. We present DeepHMap++, a novel method that integrates two distinct modules: a projection referral network and a correspondence learning network. The projection referral network generates synthetic images containing referral points, which are used as inputs to the correspondence learning network. The latter employs a siamese architecture to learn a similarity metric between the synthetic images and the input image. We leverage the implicit learning of DoF via correspondence and incorporate 3D object descriptors into the siamese network. Experimentation on the BOP Challenge dataset confirms the superiority of our approach in estimating 6D object poses.

We present GGLasso, a Python-based framework for Generalized Graphical Lasso
computation. Generalized Graphical Lasso encompasses various inverse
problems involving undirected graphs, such as covariance estimation, inverse
covariance estimation, and multiple spike and slab regression. We introduce
new algorithms for solving several graphical Lasso variants, including
semidefinite programming for covariance estimation and its sparse alternative,
as well as an iterative thresholding method for multiple spike and slab
regression. We also address model selection for Generalized Graphical Lasso
via an penalized version of the BIC criterion, and provide an empirical study
of GGLasso on synthetic and real-world data.

To enhance the efficiency of molecular sampling in molecular dynamics simulations, we've developed an optimized method for handling collisions with walls in Langevin dynamics.  By taking into account the momenta of atoms relative to their bonds, we've created a robust and versatile technique for simulating particle configurations and determining their fluctuations.  This approach, known as Refined Gamma Distribution (RGD), compares the distribution of configurational gamma variables to a reference set, which serves as a benchmark against which the accuracy of our method is measured.  We've demonstrated the versatility and effectiveness of RGD by applying it to a diverse range of simulations, including polymer chains, biomolecules, chemical reactions, and phase transition phenomena, as well as multiple dimensions and bond types.  Our results show that RGD yields precise results while using a minimal number of configurational samples, outperforming existing methods such as Gaussian distribution-based approaches and providing a straightforward means of incorporating prior knowledge of particle configurations.

Our new approach assigns a distinct significance value to each node in a multilayer network based on its eigenvalue and prominence. This value represents how prominently the node's layer contributes to the network's overall structure. As the threshold $\lambda$ that determines significance increases, more isolated nodes with smaller eigenvalues are considered insignificant. In contrast to existing methods that focus on a single layer or treat layers as interconnected but independent components, our approach leverages the interconnectedness of layers to define significance. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by applying it to three distinct multilayer networks, each representing a different type of interconnection between layers, and analyze the resulting significance values to identify patterns of layer connectivity.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using the Finsler geometry approach, 
which leads to the $R$-Minkowski spacetime. In this study, we derive the Dirac equation 
within the context of $R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish its differential operator 
form. It is demonstrated that the conventional Dirac operator is not a representation 
of the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra. Furthermore, we provide a novel interpretation of the 
Gupta-Kibble-Schwinger effect within the framework of $R$-Minkowski spacetime.

This study utilizes high-speed imaging to examine spheres interacting with a plane water surface, specifically in the moderate regime between static and rolling states. A newly introduced dimensionless parameter, the surface shear regime number, is crucial in understanding this interfacial dynamics. Observations reveal that the static to rolling transition is characterized by a spiral pattern on the surface, while lower speed regimes exhibit spiral patterns that eventually give way to rolling through a stationary drop formation. The occurrence of this transition is influenced by the sphere's size, surface tension, and water density. Furthermore, the formation of the rolling state is complex, with different sphere sizes exhibiting either a single-drop or a double-drop formation regime. The condition for a single-drop or double-drop formations is defined by the water density and sphere diameter parameters. This research also introduces a new seal pattern called the annular ring pattern, which surrounds the sphere as it rolls. This pattern can switch between the surface shear regime number ranges of the static and rolling states.

A well-known $\theta$-term in Type IIB supergravity undergoes modifications when accounted for at a lower energy scale, as it becomes part of a more comprehensive $\theta$-term sector that includes an additional, locally varying component. This adjustment results in the $\theta$-term sector being described by a complex, vector-field-strength-triple $\theta$-term, thereby ensuring consistency with local gauge invariance. Furthermore, this reformulation yields a novel, locally-defined Weyl-weight $\theta$-term for each distinct irreducible representation of the local gauge group, effectively generating Weyl-weight $\theta$-terms for all possible representations through a process of conformal transformation. When applied to a specific scenario involving a $U(1)$ local gauge symmetry with charged scalar fields, this development results in the creation of a $\theta$-term that acts to break the local symmetry spontaneously, thereby relating to the development of a monopole particle associated with this symmetry.

Our study employs theoretical and experimental methods to investigate the orbital properties of cupricite, a rare mineral comprising copper and iron sulfides. Through a combination of first-principles calculations, spectroscopic analysis, and crystallographic study, we have determined the oxidation states of iron within the compound and identified localized $3d$ electrons in the $\Gamma$ and M points of the Brillouin zone. We have also identified both filled and empty bands of iron in the compound, which is uncommon. Our findings are supported by experimental data from X-ray absorption near edges, X-ray photoemission, and spectroscopy, as well as crystallographic structural refinement. We have further explored the magnetic properties of cupricite and identified both itinerant and localized magnetic moments in the compound, which is consistent with our experimental measurements of magnetization and specific heat. Our research indicates that cupricite exhibits both Mott-Hubbard and itinerant behavior, which is extremely rare in natural minerals.

A significant phenomenon known as Rabi oscillation between different quantum states can occur due to the interaction between an external magnetic field and a specific energy level. This research focuses on theoretical modeling to achieve enormous Rabi oscillations between an unbound exciton state and a bound exciton state within an optically active, semiconducting material, despite the lack of an applied magnetic field. Unlike usual approaches, our method involves utilizing an intense light pulse that causes a huge shift in the energy levels instead of relying on an external magnetic field for this effect. By employing a multi-quantum cell approach and identifying crucial parameters through calculations based on microscopic properties, we were able to derive a specific condition that can lead to enormous Rabi oscillations between the two exciton states. Furthermore, we demonstrated that this model is applicable to a particular type of semiconductor material known as WSe2, thereby providing the groundwork for experimental verification of this phenomenon.

A type of two-dimensional lattice known as a non-symmorphic wallpaper structure holds exceptional potential for the creation of adjustable Dirac points with varying gap sizes, due to the unique cross-sectional structure of its Brillouin zone. We have the capability to tailor the band structure of this lattice using an external electric field, which allows us to position Dirac points at desired locations within the spectrum. Notably, by applying a critical field strength, we can separate the Dirac points into individual masses, resulting in massless and massive gapless phases. The framework of this non-symmorphic wallpaper structure also enables us to adjust the orientation of the conical surfaces surrounding the points, further enhancing its unique properties. Our proposed design exhibits robustness in its electronic structure, demonstrating promising applications in the development of massless or massive Dirac fermion systems.

Quantum states known as single-photon facilitated coherent states possess unique properties like resistance to sudden death and coherent destruction of quantum fluctuations, making them beneficial for quantum information processing tasks. We've demonstrated the capability of utilizing a quantum oscillator's nonlinear interaction with annihilation and creation operators to generate these states via quantum-optical catalysis, facilitated by a single photon. This process allows for the creation of a coherent state that resists the entanglement-swap death caused by interacting with an unknown oscillator, thus making it suitable for executing precise quantum operations on the unknown oscillator. Calculations performed theoretically also confirmed the feasibility of this process, showing that even when the oscillator's initial state is a Fock state or a Gaussian state, the generated state still exhibits resistance to sudden death and coherent destruction of quantum fluctuations.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the exact solutions of Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose 32-component formalism, specifically by translating the electromagnetic tensor into its respective complex bivector components. Additionally, we derive the Weyl curvature tensor's matrix elements from their corresponding complex bivector components.

A new method for creating polynomial equations is proposed, building on the foundations of linear regression and integer optimization. This technique enables the generation of precise polynomial representations for given data points, ensuring consistency through validation processes. Unlike other methods, this approach avoids issues of overfitting and ensures generated polynomials are both realistic and realistic-sounding to human listeners. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique by applying it to the creation of artificial patient data for training and evaluating a medical prediction model.

We developed an innovative medical image segmentation technology, incorporating attention mechanisms and dense connections to enhance performance. Our novel model, known as Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet), applies two types of attention techniques to prioritize crucial data features for both spatial and channel representations, thereby improving efficiency. We further introduced a dense connection structure between the inner layers of our unet architecture to facilitate the free exchange of information between different layers, reducing redundancy. Our DDAUnet model was specifically designed to detect neoplasms in CT images of the esophagus, yielding a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.79, a mean surface distance of 12.8 mm, and a mean absolute surface distance of 24.3 mm when compared to traditional radiation therapy treatment plans. Our findings indicate that our model excels in both surgical and radiological assessments, surpassing the current state-of-the-art performance in our targeted task.

Multilingual individuals possess proficiency in two or more languages, enabling them to read and write in each language, including code-switching and code-mixing. While prior research considered code-switching as speech error, current studies view it as a language resource with immense potential. This paper delves into the world of multilingual NLP, exploring theoretical frameworks such as language representation, acquisition, and use, as well as empirical studies on multilingual children's language development. Furthermore, we examine current NLP models and their limitations in handling multilingualism. Leveraging insights from psychology and linguistics, we discuss actionable suggestions to enhance the performance of NLP systems for code-switching and multilingual tasks.

Standardizing the description of visual contents across various texts is a longstanding goal in computer vision. This endeavor's success hinges on the quality of its reference data. Typically, reference datasets are created through a crowdsourcing process where participants describe the same images using their own words. This approach is often speedy but may compromise the consistency and reliability of the resulting data. In contrast, using expert annotators with in-depth knowledge of the target application can create more precise and consistent descriptions but often takes far longer to complete. Despite expert-annotated datasets being less common due to their time-consuming creation, they are nonetheless usable for training models. In fact, using such datasets for model evaluation can be particularly valuable as they more closely resemble the type of accuracy that matters most to developers. Interestingly enough, there is little research on this precise topic. As a result, we are launching a new dataset called HumanReferenceForObjectDetection that leverages expert-annotated descriptions of images to assess the quality of automatic image description models. This dataset's primary focus is on the field of object detection, yet its methodology is versatile enough to be applied to other description tasks as well.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values, minimal refractive index variation, and transparent crystal structures. As a result of these characteristics, Ta$_2$O$_5$ is utilized in various applications such as optical coatings, semiconducting devices, and ceramic manufacturing. Nevertheless, research on these substances is complicated by the presence of multiple polymorphs, which pose a problem in evaluating and predicting their physical characteristics. We have carried out theoretical calculations using the generalized gradient approximation plus $U$ method and Monte Carlo simulations at finite temperatures to investigate different Ta$_2$O$_5$ polymorphs, and have been able to reproduce experimental lattice parameters and tauntenizing energies. Furthermore, we have been able to predict the stable state of the substance at finite temperatures, and have investigated how its stability is affected by both lattice parameters and tauntenizing energies.

Researchers analyzed the spread of misinformation on Reddit, focusing on the role of users' physical locations, which were inferred based on user-submitted images and comments. A notable correlation was found between users' geographic distances from major population centers, known as the Big Sort, and their susceptibility to falling prey to false information. Users residing in urban areas were found to be more likely to encounter and believe in false information. However, users from these areas were also more likely to engage in fact-checking. In contrast, users from rural areas were more likely to adhere to presented information, regardless of its accuracy. The study identified key differences in behavior between users from urban and rural areas, which could be attributed to social connections and access to information. The results also highlight the negative consequences of the Big Sort, namely the increased dissemination of misinformation in urban areas.

Humans effortlessly grasp complex auditory feedback from instructors guiding them through robotic manipulations. Despite the ease with which this happens, the underlying processes shaping these auditory cues remain poorly understood. We set out to investigate how the sound of an instructor's voice is affected by the robotic arm's position, with the aim of creating more effective listening-based learning experiences. In a controlled setting, a participant was shown a robotic arm performing a specific task, with the instructor providing verbal guidance. We then analyzed how the sound of the voice was impacted by the robotic arm's configuration. Our findings show that instructors exhibit distinct patterns in the pitch and volume of their voice in response to the robotic arm's position. What's particularly noteworthy is that these patterns vary greatly from one instructor to the next. Based on our observations, we propose that the acoustic cues provided by an instructor's voice are influenced by the relationship between the robotic arm's end-effector and the task it is performing, as defined by the robot's joints. What's more, this relationship can be different for each joint, and this variability could be a key factor in the lack of consensus among previous studies. What's next is to put these findings into practice by developing a way to forecast the acoustic cues based on the robot's configuration, and to incorporate this forecasting capability into a system that can teach a robot a new task via auditory feedback.

A set of intricate differential equations, known as Euler-Arnold equations and their Hamiltonian counterparts, serve as the foundation for conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions. These equations encompass a broad range of phenomena, from random walks to conformal field theories, and have been successfully applied to describe superdiffusive behaviors. However, the scope of Euler-Arnold equations extends far beyond this realm, as they also provide a framework for nonlinear gradient descent equations and their Hamiltonian variants. These equations can be given a Hamiltonian formulation that allows us to identify extensive conserved quantities, which in turn allows us to solve the equations and determine their behavior for both one-dimensional and two-dimensional spaces.

Conversational interfaces tied to human-like language are gaining widespread use, and as a result, the demand for a systematic approach to thoroughly examine their underlying technology is rising. Unfortunately, researchers face a significant obstacle in testing these systems due to the abstract and ever-changing nature of language, making it difficult to pinpoint issues and evaluate their solutions. A novel approach, the Conversational Bot Testing Laboratory, has been developed to address these challenges by providing a controlled environment for testing and experimenting with conversational systems. This system identifies flaws in tested systems and offers data-driven confirmation of problem existence, along with actionable feedback for developers on problem types, severity levels, and sample user interactions. The system's capability to handle multiple systems and provide customizable testing scenarios makes it an adaptable tool for various testing needs, from validating individual components to testing integrated systems across different domains.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the growing amount of multi-sparse-domain user data. Recommending products from multiple domains with limited data available for each user poses a substantial challenge. Existing methods often overlook the differences between domains and may favor domains with more data, compromising the performance for denser domains. In response, this research introduces a novel approach, MSCDR, specifically designed to address the complexities of multiple sparse domains. MSCDR builds upon the foundation of attribute preference learning by incorporating a cooperative component and imposing restrictions to account for domain variations. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through empirical testing, where it achieves superior performance in multiple sparse domains relative to baseline methods.

Conic optimization enables the resolution of diverse problems via specialized cones, which can be combined to tackle more complex challenges. Conic problems are identified by comparing their objective function, constraints, and feasible regions defined by cones, which are inherently non-convex when viewed through the lens of convexity. Given two conic problems, we can determine if one is equivalent to the other, up to convex scalability, by employing a set of rules and analyzing their underlying geometry. A computational implementation of this concept is available in the form of the Hypatia conic resolution library for Julia, which can be used as a standalone tool or incorporated into existing solvers and optimization frameworks.

The escalating use and complexity of MRI systems pose significant challenges in ensuring their accuracy, leading to an increased need for quality assurance methods. Currently, quality assurance for MRI systems relies heavily on time-consuming and labor-intensive phantom-based tests. Researchers are now exploring the potential of machine learning models to predict the performance of MRI systems based on scanned phantom data. However, such models require extensive training and data, which is often difficult to obtain, and they must also perform well in new, unseen situations, which is a crucial challenge. A study published in the journal Medical Physics has examined the capabilities of convolutional neural networks in predicting MRI image quality from scanned phantom data. The research evaluated multiple protocols and systems across various locations and found that transferring knowledge from one site to another was the most significant challenge. The study showed that transferring knowledge between different MRI systems at the same site was more feasible, although system-specific information was necessary to predict image quality. Nonetheless, transferring knowledge between locations proved to be too difficult, with a marked decline in performance of over 50%.

To assess the impact of privately owned electric vehicles on a distribution network's sustainability and resilience, a new indicator called Environmental Sustainability and Resilience (ESR) is proposed, considering the network's carbon footprint and ability to withstand disturbances and recover quickly. A multi-agent optimization approach is then developed to determine optimal management strategies for distribution networks, taking into account various stakeholders' interests and constraints. By applying this method, researchers analyzed and compared different scenarios involving private electric cars, energy storage systems, and rooftop solar power, finding that private electric cars can significantly decrease a network's carbon footprint but may also increase its vulnerability to failures and decreased overall ESR.

An intriguing theory posits that through autonomous, agent-driven social interactions, group objectives can be efficiently pursued by independent entities with disparate interests. To explore and validate this concept, an innovative model has been developed which enables multiple agents to engage in recurring meetings to discuss and determine courses of action. Each agent's decision-making process is characterized by an incentive-driven mechanism, with the outcome of their discussion influencing their individual rewards. Studies have been conducted to examine the proposed model's capabilities under both controlled and complex, dynamically changing environments, with the results demonstrating its ability to adapt and achieve optimal outcomes in a variety of scenarios.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental characteristics of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

Quark-diquark models resemble the fundamental quark-gluon interaction at high energies, where quarks and gluons are nearly independent particles due to asymptotic freedom. By applying these models, we can anticipate the behavior of quarks and gluons at very high energies. Since diquarks are constructed from the same quarks as mesons are from quarks and gluons, we can use these models to forecast the properties of extra baryons and mesons that might be discovered with the help of a 100 TeV collider or beyond. Specifically, we can analyze how the mass of the collider affects the formation of extra baryons and mesons and how their masses are influenced by the interaction between quarks and diquarks.

The Coxeter groups, fueled by their applications in mathematics and physics, have been increasingly prominent in various studies. Based on the harmonic analysis within the Heisenberg group, we have previously established a significant theorem known as the foundation theorem. This significant theorem, along with its generalization to the nilpotent groups of degree two, has been utilized in constructing the Fock space and providing a central to peripheral decomposition. In this study, we will generalize the foundation theorem to the B-type Coxeter groups of finite rank. This generalization will enable us to extend the central to peripheral decomposition theorem to this specific class of groups.
